title: Late Breaking Results: Utilization of Hybrid Threshold-Voltage Flip-flops for Power Recovery
problem: Leakage power reduction in advanced technology nodes is challenging; multi-VT optimization can reduce leakage in non-critical paths, but critical-path sequential cells resist multi-VT optimization due to timing constraints.
motivation: Leakage power dominates static power consumption at advanced nodes; enabling multi-VT optimization on timing-critical sequential elements would unlock additional power savings.
method: Flip-flops store data in two sequential parts: master and slave latches. Using slower transistors reduces power but makes both input timing (setup time) and output speed (clock-to-Q delay) worse together. This design uses faster transistors in the slave latch (to meet timing requirements on critical paths) and slower, power-saving transistors in the master latch (where input timing is less strict). This decoupled control enables power reduction throughout the design while satisfying all timing constraints.
key_novelty: First flip-flop design using different transistor speeds in master and slave latches to independently control setup time and output speed for power optimization on critical timing paths.
contributions: Novel hybrid-VT flip-flop cells with decoupled master/slave VT assignment
Independent setup time and clock-to-Q delay control
8.97% additional leakage power reduction over conventional multi-VT optimization with zero timing degradation
primary_theme: Hybrid-VT flip-flops for leakage reduction on critical paths
